title: Stewed, seasoned, ground beef and pork, Mexican style

content.title: About
content.content: Stewed, seasoned, ground beef and pork, Mexican style (1270) is a ready‑to‑eat meat blend made from beef and pork, flavored with traditional Mexican spices and slowly stewed until tender. It is convenient for tacos, burritos, chili, pie fillings and many other dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mexican seasoning typically includes chili, cumin, oregano, paprika and garlic, giving the blend its characteristic aroma.
The beef‑pork combination balances flavor: beef adds depth, pork adds juiciness.
Low‑heat stewing preserves most nutrients and makes the meat easy to digest.
The product is widely used in fast‑food outlets and cafeterias where quick preparation without flavor loss is essential.
Traditional Mexican ground meat often contains a touch of tomato paste to enhance taste.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The beef‑pork blend provides a rich source of complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat supplies heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat is abundant in vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Beneficial fats
items.content: Pork contributes monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that are important for heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Chili and cumin contain antioxidant compounds that may help reduce inflammation.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Seasonings can add salt; people monitoring sodium intake should account for this in their overall diet.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Pork adds saturated fat; moderate consumption is advised for those with cardiovascular concerns.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to chili, coriander or other spices used in the blend.

items.title: Requires thorough cooking
items.content: To eliminate pathogenic bacteria, the meat should be heated to an internal temperature of at least 71 °C (160 °F).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The product is ready for use after reheating. Add it to tacos, burritos, chili, soups, casseroles, or use as a filling for peppers or tortillas. For extra brightness, top with fresh cilantro, lime juice and avocado.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store refrigerated at 0–4 °C in the original packaging for up to 5 days after opening. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly before consumption.
